recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed unless a future work-group decision requests additional HumanName examples or Practitioner-specific name guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-3500 asked for a way to represent health-worker/practitioner names with needed structured components, including clearer HumanName mapping guidance and consideration of repeated practitioner names rather than repeated HumanName.text.
initial_application: The HumanName documentation portion was applied by 77004cea3f6efea47c635074f2b8ff2d5680c1ad, which added HumanName clarifications and international examples. The Practitioner.name repeatability portion was applied through FHIR-9067 by 64afb1d0b601aca0cd926438c18e5ca11ddbf6ab, which changed Practitioner.name to 0..* and added display-name selection guidance.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini keeps HumanName and Practitioner in active build scope. Current HumanName prose and examples include common part mapping, alternate-name guidance, culture-dependent ordering, text-versus-parts robustness, family-name decomposition guidance, and extensive examples. Later FHIR-12351 reworked HumanName.family to one family string plus decomposition extensions and is already audited on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current source already carries the requested guidance and cardinality outcome. No source edit is needed, and restoring older repeated-family examples would conflict with later HumanName rework.

related_jiras.note: Confirms and applies the Practitioner.name 0..* and display guidance portion called out in FHIR-3500's resolution.
Reworked HumanName family-name decomposition after FHIR-3500 and explains the current 0..1 family plus extension guidance; it is already represented on the combined branch.
